scenes.heading: Fossil evidence
scenes.sub: How do we know how old a fossil is?
scenes.say: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of organisms that lived long ago. They show how life has changed. But how do scientists work out how old they are?

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Only a few party photos survive, mostly of people near the camera
scenes.science: Only a few organisms become fossils, mostly those with hard parts
scenes.breaks: a photo takes an instant, but fossilisation usually takes a very long time as minerals slowly replace the original material.
scenes.say: At a big party, most moments are never photographed, and many photos get lost. The fossil record is the same. Most organisms are eaten or decompose. Fossils usually form from organisms with hard parts, buried quickly in low-oxygen sediment. So the record is incomplete and biased.

scenes.heading: Relative dating
points: Easy to identify, short time span
Gives the order, not an age in years
scenes.say: Relative dating puts fossils in order. By superposition, lower layers are older, like a laundry pile. Index fossils are widespread, abundant, easy to identify and lived for a short time. Finding one in different places means those layers are about the same age.

scenes.heading: Radiometric dating
parts: time for half the parent isotope to decay
scenes.say: Absolute dating gives an age in years. A radioactive parent isotope decays into a daughter isotope at a constant rate. The half-life is the time for half the parent to decay. Age equals the number of half-lives times the length of one half-life.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A bone has 1/8 of the carbon-14 in living bone. The half-life of ¹⁴C is 5730 years. How old is it?
scenes.say: A bone has one eighth of its carbon fourteen left. Halve, count, multiply. One, a half, a quarter, an eighth: that's three half-lives. Three times five thousand seven hundred and thirty gives seventeen thousand one hundred and ninety years.
scenes.caption: A bone has 1/8 of its carbon-14 left. Halve, count, multiply. 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8: that's 3 half-lives. 3 × 5730 gives 17 190 years.

scenes.heading: Which isotope?
scenes.say: Carbon fourteen is for the recently dead. It dates organic remains up to about fifty thousand years old. Dinosaurs are far older, so scientists date the volcanic layers above and below them using potassium forty or uranium two thirty-eight.
scenes.caption: Carbon-14 is for the recently dead. It dates organic remains up to about 50 000 years old. Dinosaurs are far older, so scientists date the volcanic layers above and below them using potassium-40 or uranium-238.

scenes.heading: Transitional fossils
points: Mix of ancestral and descendant features
Archaeopteryx: feathers plus teeth and tail
Tiktaalik: fish with a neck and wrist bones
scenes.say: Transitional fossils mix features of an ancestral group and a later group. Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings, but also teeth, clawed fingers and a long bony tail. Tiktaalik was a fish with a neck and wrist-like fin bones.

points: Fossils need rapid burial, low oxygen
scenes.say: Quick recap. Fossils are rare, so the record is incomplete. Relative dating gives the order. Radiometric dating gives an age using half-lives. Carbon fourteen is for young remains. Now try the practice questions!
